cells.tense: You are working in the clear, and the work is yours, and it holds.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Put the steps you actually take when the work matters onto one page, in order, no commentary — then work from that page next time rather than from your mood.
cells.core:
The clearing has already done its job. Whatever structure couldn't hold came down, and what's left standing is real. You can go a whole afternoon without arguing yourself into the work — you sit down and the thing is sound, and the soundness is the reason the afternoon went somewhere. The work runs on what's true about it rather than on what you can summon.

What keeps it there is the method you already have. Put your own steps on one page, in the order you take them, without feeling words. Then follow the page the next time the work gets hard instead of deciding from how the morning feels. The page asks nothing of your mood.

cells.verb: pioneering the clearing of what can't hold

cells.tense: You are braced ahead of a clearing that has not happened yet.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Before the next thing comes down, say out loud to the person it concerns the one true reason it matters to you — no case attached.
cells.core:
You can already see it down the road. The structure you think is false, the clean break, the version of the work you'll have once the dust settles — it's all vivid ahead of you, and the day you're actually in gets spent bracing for it. The clearing hasn't happened yet, and the waiting is doing the work of the doing.

Saying why it matters is a different act, and you skip it. Before the next thing comes down, tell the person it concerns one true thing about why it does — no speech, one sentence that is actually so. The break stops being a performance in your head, and the reasoning gets somewhere to live. Then the day you're in can hold you again.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door the collapse already took down.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Choose an hour of the week that stays yours, say so once, and hold it without explaining — no case, no apology.
cells.core:
Behind you, something came down. There's one thing here that no one has cleared: a limit you set once, gave back, and haven't set again since. The days fill with what other people planned, and the hours you agreed to are hard to tell apart from the ones you chose. The break you could spot a mile off is one you keep not making.

Set one small boundary and hold it. No speech, no case — an hour that stays yours, kept for a week. It doesn't need a plan for the next month. It needs to look like the same thing on a camera. When the wall holds, you can be inside it, and the clearing stops waiting on someone else.

cells.tense: You are building the thing and calling it someone else's plan.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Feed the interest a little at a time this week — start the work when it's actually there, no pushing through on empty.
cells.core:
The clearing happens through your hands, and the story is that it's just how the work goes. The hours spent taking things apart and putting them back, the version of the thing that keeps getting clearer — you do it, and you say it's circumstance, or the moment, or someone else's direction. It doesn't feel like yours, so you don't claim it.

Move when the interest is actually in you. That's the whole instruction. Before you start, wait until the want is there — no acting on empty, no pushing through to prove something — and then do it. A fire stays bright when it's fed a little at a time. Carried instead of fed, it burns on the wrong surface and the moving goes leaden.

attempts.check: The record supports writing structure down and following it, but not that the person's life is unusually orderly or that a discipline they can name already exists. A reader could reasonably say the method was never theirs to begin with, that it belonged to a school or an employer or a family script. The ask survives: journalling the method once, by hand, is useful even if the whole reading is wrong about what it means. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one about carrying what was built — it is a posture I find satisfying, and I have trimmed it back.
